Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a complex problem by calling itself to break the task down into smaller, more manageable pieces. You can think of it like Russian nesting dolls, where opening one doll reveals a smaller version of itself inside, repeating the process until you reach the tiniest doll. To prevent the function from calling itself forever and crashing your computer, it must include a "base case" that stops the repetition once the simplest version of the problem is reached. Finally, as each smaller sub-problem is solved, the results bubble back up through the chain of function calls to assemble the final answer to the original problem.
